works.abstract: Microplastics are increasingly recognized as emerging contaminants in freshwater environments; however, data remain limited for karst aquifer systems such as those of the Yucatán Peninsula, Mexico. Through a Research Experience for Undergraduates (REU) program, this study investigated the presence and characteristics of microplastics in sinkholes, locally known as cenotes, and pozos (drinking water wells) to better understand microplastic occurrence in vulnerable karst settings. Sampling locations were selected to represent different freshwater environments within the karst system and drinking water sources used by local communities. Water samples were collected and processed using standardized extraction protocols, including pre-filtration, hydrogen peroxide digestion, zinc chloride density separation, and final filtration onto gold-coated membranes. Microplastic particles were identified and quantified using a Laser Direct Infrared (LDIR) chemical imaging system, enabling polymer identification and particle size characterization. Microplastics were detected in all sampled environments, with particles < 100 µm dominating the samples. The most frequently identified polymers included polyethylene terephthalate (PET), polyamide (PA), polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE), and polyurethane (PU). Differences in microplastic abundance and polymer composition were observed between cenote waters and drinking water sources, suggesting the influence of hydrology, land use, and local infrastructure on microplastic distribution in karst systems. Beyond generating baseline data, this project provided hands-on training for undergraduate researchers in field sampling, laboratory processing, and advanced microplastics analysis. The integration of undergraduate research and mentorship enhanced research capacity while contributing valuable data on microplastics in groundwater-connected freshwater systems and that in the end could be a contaminant that affects human health. These findings highlight the need for continued monitoring of microplastics in environmentally sensitive karst regions.

works.title: Microplastics in Freshwater Karst Systems of the Yucatán Peninsula
